December 1, 1933. 4 Afternoon Translation.

The Free Comment (自由評論), a bi-monthly periodical, published
the following article in its 21st issue, Vol. 1 dated Dec. 1.

FAILURE OF THE STRIKE IN THE SHANGHAI POWER CO.

The strikers in the Shanghai Power Company,
who supported the movement for a period of two months,
have now been obliged resume work, except for 50 enthu-
siasts who refused to resume/were dismissed.
The company has not issued wages for the .
period of the strike but has issued one month's pay to
each worker as a loan which must be refunded. Thus the
strike was a failure.
Why did the strikers fail? The Shanghai
Power Co. is one of the organizations belonging to
the American imperialists who have robbed China of her
rights. Residents in the Settlement have to pay heavy
electricity bills every month and are also oppressed by
the company. The Shanghai Power Co. is a part of a
company in America which has a capital of G.$3,000,000,000
and it is useless to struggle against capitalism.
Only a few compradores, traitors, running
dogs and militarists succeed when working for the
capitalists while the toiling masses and residents suffer
grief.

《自由评论》（The Free Comment），一份双周刊，在其第一卷第二十一期（12月1日出版）中发表了以下文章。

上海电力公司罢工失败

上海电力公司的罢工者支持此次运动达两个月之久，现除50名拒绝复工或被解雇的热心分子外，其余人员均被迫复工。公司在罢工期间未发放工资，但向每位工人发放相当于一个月工资的贷款，该款项必须偿还。因此，此次罢工以失败告终。

罢工者为何失败？上海电力公司是掠夺中国权利的美国帝国主义者的所属机构之一。租界居民每月须支付高昂的电费，并受该公司压迫。上海电力公司是一家美国公司的分部，该美国公司资本高达30亿美元，对抗资本主义是徒劳的。只有少数为资本家效力的买办、汉奸、走狗和军阀获得成功，而劳苦大众和居民则遭受苦难。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, November 25, 1933

Power Company Men
Holding General Meet
Shanghai Power Company work-
ers were to meet at offices of the
Nantao Tramway Employees' Union,
Kuo Hwo Road, Nantao, at 2 o'clock
this afternoon to discuss the
various issues following their re-
sumption of work on Wednesday
after a two-month strike.
Resuming their work under the
misapprehension that they were to
be paid one month's wages for the
period of the strike, the workers
expressed dissatisfaction with the
union when they discovered they
were only allowed to borrow from
the company. The discussions this
afternoon were to be centered on
that question, it is understood.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》（The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury），1933年11月25日，星期六

电力公司员工
举行全体会议

上海电力公司员工定于今日下午2时在南市国货路（Kuo Hwo Road）南市电车工会办事处集会，讨论在为期两个月的罢工后于周三复工后的各项事宜。

工人们复工时误以为将获得相当于罢工期间一个月工资的薪酬，当发现仅被允许向公司借款时，他们对工会表示不满。据悉，今日的讨论将集中于该问题。

November 26, 1933. Morning Translation

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

THE S.P.C. WORKERS

About 100 workers of both the new and old
plants of the Shanghai Power Company attended a meeting
held at 3 p.m. yesterday in the premises of the 1st
District Waterworks & Electricity Trade Workers Union,
Nantao. Officials from the local Tangpu, the Social
Bureau and the General Labour Union were also present.

During the function, the circumstances
leading to the settlement of the trouble and the conditions
during the resumption of work were reported.

Important proposals were then discussed and
it is learned that the mediators will be urged to continue
the negotiations with the Company.

November 25, 1933. Morning Translation

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

S.P.C. WORKERS TO HOLD MEETING.

Through the good offices of Mr. Doo Yueh-sun,
member of the Council of the Chinese Municipality, Messrs.
Yuan Lee-tung, Yu Yah-ching, Zee Hsin-loh, Chinese members
of the Shanghai Municipal Council, Wong Shao-lai, chairman
of the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce, and others,
the strikers of both the old and the new plants of the
Shanghai Power Company resumed duty on the morning of
November 22 and the management yesterday issued to each
worker a loan equivalent to one month's pay.
The entire body of workers will hold a meeting
at 2 p.m. to-day in the premises of the Nantao Tramway
Company Workers Union, Kuo Fu Road, Nantao. A petition has
been submitted to the local Tangpu and the General Labour
Union requesting them to detail officials to preside at
the function.
According to a responsible member of the General
Labour Union, proposals will be submitted to the Company
following further discussions between Mr. Doo Yueh-sun and
the Chinese members of the S.M.C.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

THE WORKERS OF THE CANTON BROTHERS VULCANIZING
WORKS.

With reference to the labour trouble in the
Canton Brothers Vulcanizing Works, Baikal Road, the 4th
District Vulcanizing Trade Workers Union, upon receipt of
instructions from the Social Bureau, immediately advised
the hands to resume work and await a settlement.
Yesterday morning, the management refused to
allow the workers to resume, and stated that only the hands
who were selected would be allowed to resume.
The Union then detailed an official to submit
an appeal to the Social Bureau.

China Times and other local newspapers:

THE SAN YEU TOWEL FACTORY

With reference to the dispute between the San Yeu
Towel Factory and their employees, in addition to a joint
petition addressed by nine native goods factory organisations
to the Central Kuomintang Headquarters, the Executive Yuan,
Ministries of Justice and Industry, it is understood that
the management has decided to file an appeal against the
decision in the Supreme Court of the country at Nanking.

Shanghai Power Company - situation

The situation at Riverside and Fearon Road
Power Stations continues normal,

Unemployed Workers' Group of Silver Melting
Trade - delegates appeal to the Chinese Authorities

Forty-eight Chinese claiming to represent the
unemployed workers of the silver melting trade called
at the local Kuomintang and the Bureau of Social Affairs
in the morning of November 24 and requested the
Authorities to assist them in negotiating with the
Traders' Association the sale of the Silver Melting
Guild (South Chen Dah Loong (南陳大弄)) off Tiendong
Road, Chapei, and all properties belonging to this

concerns suspended business in October on the instructions

business interfered with the operations of the Central

workers in the trade formed a Group in the offices of
Tu Tseng Kao (屠徵鵠) and Tsang Ting (張挺), two legal
advisors of the body with offices on the second floor of
the Industrial Bank of China, 172 Nanking Road.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 22
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
S. 9. REGI
No. D
Date / /

POWER CO. WORKERS
APPLY FOR LOANS
Little Enthusiasm Over
Plan; Russians Will
Be Discharged

Practically all of the 1,500 employees of the Shanghai Power Company, who returned to work on Wednesday morning after a strike which lasted 54 days, are expected to take advantage of the loan of one month's pay which the Company has offered, according to Chinese reports. Little enthusiasm was shown, however, over the arrangement. Some 360 Russian workers, who filled the positions of the striking employees, will be discharged on Saturday, according to the same source, and each of these men will be paid a bonus of two weeks wages.

No untoward incidents happened on Wednesday morning when the workers resumed duty, but none of the 60 workers, discharged by the Company as agitators, reported at the premises for their retiring gratuities and other payments. It is reported that negotiations over these payments will be opened by mediators in the near future.

The workers returned upon the conditions laid down by the Company, but were reinstated without loss of service credits or benefits previously earned. Wages earned up to date of the strike will be paid and all of those desiring a loan of one month's wages will be accommodated. This latter payment will be made without interest charges and will be refunded to the Company by deduction of 10 per cent. of earned wages beginning in February.

（批：拟）
（批：11/24）

电力公司员工
申请贷款
对该计划反应冷淡；俄籍员工将被解雇

据中文报道，上海电力公司1500名员工在经历了为期54天的罢工后于周三上午复工，预计几乎所有员工都将利用公司提供的一个月工资贷款。然而，人们对该安排反应冷淡。据同一消息来源称，约360名填补罢工员工职位的俄籍工人将于周六被解雇，每人将获得相当于两周工资的奖金。

周三上午工人复工时未发生任何意外事件，但被公司作为煽动者解雇的60名工人中，无人到办公地点领取退休金及其他款项。据报道，调解人将在近期就这些款项开启谈判。

工人按照公司规定的条件返回，但复职时未损失此前累积的服务年限或福利。截至罢工开始日的工资将予支付，所有希望获得一个月工资贷款的员工都将得到满足。后一笔款项不计利息，将从二月份起通过扣除所获工资的10%偿还给公司。

（批：拟）
（批：11/24）

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 23, 1933

Power Strike
Ends As Men
Back On Job

Longest Utility Strike
In Years Collapses;
Fair Terms Granted By
Company To Employees

The 55-day strike of the Shanghai
Power Company workers was
brought to an end yesterday morn-
ing with the return of all the strik-
ing workers except 56 whom the
company has decided not to take
back. Thus the city is relieved of
one of the longest strikes ever re-
corded here during the last few
years.

In order to assist financially
employees who have been on strike,
those employees who reported for
work yesterday and were re-engaged
by the company will be accorded
the following treatment:

1. They will be reinstated with-
out loss of service credits or loss
of any benefits that they have
earned.

2. Wages earned up to date of
strike will be paid upon return.

3. Those who want a loan will
be advanced one month's pay from
retirement gratuity that they have
earned. Such advance is made
without interest charge and will be
refunded to the company by the
deduction of 10 percent of the earn-
ed wages beginning with February
pay-day.

（批：Juli R.）
（右上角手写：6.5--）
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》（THE CHINA PRESS），1933年11月23日，星期四

电力罢工
随员工返岗
而结束

多年来最长的公用事业罢工瓦解；
公司向员工提供公平条款

上海电力公司工人的55天罢工于昨日上午随着除56名公司决定不予录用的罢工者外的所有罢工工人返岗而宣告结束。至此，本市摆脱了近几年来记录在案的最长罢工之一。

为了在财政上援助一直罢工的雇员，那些昨日报到并被公司重新聘用的雇员将获得以下待遇：

1. 他们将复职，不损失服务年限或已获得的任何福利。

2. 截至罢工开始日的工资将在返岗时支付。

3. 需要贷款者将从其已获得的退休金中预支一个月工资。此类预支不计利息，将从二月份发薪日起通过扣除所获工资的10%偿还给公司。

（批：Juli R.）
（右上角手写：6.5--）

November 23, 1933. Morning Translations

LABOUR.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

S.P.C. STRIKERS RESUME WORK.

With reference to the labour trouble in the Shanghai Power Company, the entire body of strikers resumed work yesterday morning.
Prior to the resumption, the Company issued a notice declaring that old hands would be given favourable terms of employment and a loan equivalent to one month's pay.
The strikers of the new and the old plants gradually resumed by 7 a.m. yesterday. Fearing that untoward incidents might occur during the resumption, the Company requested the Police to detail policemen and detectives to be posted at the gates of the plants to afford protection. The strikers returned to duty in good order and no incidents happened.
It is reported that about 60 workers whose return has been rejected by the management did not report for duty yesterday. Negotiations over the payment of retiring gratuities and superannuation will be opened by the mediators.
With a view to reporting on the circumstances leading to the settlement of the dispute and future plans, the 4th District Waterworks & Electricity Trade Workers Union will hold a general meeting on November 25 in the premises of the Nantao Tramway Company Workers Union, Nantao. A petition has been submitted to the General Labour Union, the local Tangpu and other political organs to detail officials to tender advice at the meeting.

劳工事务。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

上海电力公司罢工者复工。

关于上海电力公司（Shanghai Power Company）的劳资纠纷，全体罢工人员于昨日上午复工。
在复工之前，该公司发布通告，声明老员工将获得优惠的雇佣条件，以及相当于一个月薪水的贷款。
新厂和旧厂的罢工者于昨日早晨7点前陆续复工。由于担心复工期间可能发生不测事件，公司请求警方派遣警员和侦探驻守工厂大门以提供保护。罢工者秩序井然地返回岗位，未发生任何事件。
据悉，约60名被管理层拒绝返聘的工人昨日未报到上班。调解人将就支付退休金和养老金的問題展开谈判。
为了报告导致争端解决的情况及未来计划，第四区水电业工会将于11月25日在南市电车公司工会会所举行全体会议。已向总工会、当地汤浦及其他政治机关提交请愿书，要求派遣官员出席会议并提供指导。

No. D
Date

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 22, 1933

Settlement Of Power Strike
Expected This Morning

Majority Of Striking Employees Expected To
Return To Work On Conditions Agreed Upon
At Representatives' Conference

Following weeks of bickering, idleness and indignation the remaining workers of the Shanghai Power Company, numbering approximately 1,500, are expected to resume duties at the Company's plants this morning and call an end to the strike which has lasted since September 29. Efforts of a number of persons who interested themselves in finding a solution to the dispute culminated on Monday evening in an agreement whereby those workers who were willing to return to duty by this morning would be taken back at the discretion of the management. Certain known agitators responsible for the walk-out, however, will not under any consideration be allowed to enter the work.

On Monday afternoon, representatives of the workers and the management of the Power Company met to discuss terms of settlement and Mr. Stirling Fessenden, Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal Council, was present at the request of both parties, but not in any official capacity. As the outcome of the conference an understanding was reached whereby the workers agreed to abide by the decisions made by their representatives. Following the conference the workers held a meeting at which it was decided that work would be resumed on Wednesday morning when strikers would present themselves at Riverside Station for re-engagement at the discretion of the management.

Advances Promised
Although the terms of settlement of the dispute have not been announced it is understood that the management has refused to pay any wages during the period of the strike, but will agree to advance one month's salary to workers requiring the money, the sum to be repaid by small amounts over a period of months. Certain guarantees regarding other payments to the strikers were given by influential Chinese who interested themselves in the settlement of the dispute.

It will be recalled that the strike commenced on September 29 when approximately 600 workers of the Riverside Station refused duty and declared a go-slow strike which developed into a walk-out. In the early stages about 2,000 workers were involved, but the Company's organization and enlistment of Russian labour prevented any dislocation of the service to the community. Several hundred of the workers returned when the Company offered them reinstatement by a given date, but the majority continued to absent themselves under threats from agitators and members of the union.

The Company throughout adopted a definite attitude and refused to give way to the demands of the strikers and it was not until Monday that the officials showed any inclination to relent. Throughout, the Company officials made it perfectly clear that they would take back workers who presented themselves, providing they were not among the list of agitators earmarked for dismissal. These men will not be given their jobs when the general return to duty commences this morning.

（批：JBR 22/11.）

《字林西报》，1933年11月22日，星期三

预计今晨解决电力公司罢工

大多数罢工员工预计将根据代表会议达成的条件复工

经过数周的争吵、怠工和愤慨之后，上海电力公司剩余的约1500名工人预计将于今晨在公司厂房恢复工作，从而结束自9月29日以来持续的罢工。许多致力于寻求解决争端方案的人士的努力，于周一晚上达成了一项协议，根据该协议，愿意在今晨之前复工的工人将由管理层酌情重新录用。然而，某些对此次停工负责的已知煽动者，在任何情况下都不允许进入工厂工作。

周一下午，工人代表与电力公司管理层会面讨论和解条款，应双方要求，上海公共租界工部局总办费信惇（Stirling Fessenden）先生出席了会议，但并非以官方身份。会议的结果是达成了一项谅解，工人同意遵守其代表作出的决定。会后，工人举行了一次会议，决定于周三上午复工，届时罢工者将前往江边电站（Riverside Station），由管理层酌情重新雇用。

承诺预支款项

虽然尚未公布争端解决的具体条款，但据了解，管理层拒绝支付罢工期间的任何工资，但同意向急需资金的工人预支一个月薪水，该款项将在数月内分期偿还。一些有影响力的中国人参与了争端的调解，并就向罢工者支付其他款项提供了某些保证。

回想起来，罢工始于9月29日，当时江边电站约600名工人拒绝履行职责，宣布进行“慢工”罢工，随后演变为全面停工。在初期，约有2000名工人卷入其中，但公司的组织工作和对俄国劳动力的招募防止了对社区服务的任何中断。当公司提出在一定日期前恢复他们的工作时，数百名工人返回，但大多数人在煽动者和工会成员的威胁下继续缺勤。

公司 throughout 采取了坚定的态度，拒绝让步于罢工者的要求，直到周一，官员们才表现出任何缓和的倾向。 throughout，公司官员明确表示，只要不在被标记为开除的煽动者名单上，他们将重新录用前来报到的工人。这些人将不会在今晨开始的大规模复工中获得工作。

（批注：JBR 11月22日。）

November 22, 1933.    Morning Translation.

LABOUR.

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

S.P.C. STRIKERS TO RESUME TO-DAY.

The "Go-slow" Strike Committee of the 4th District Waterworks & Electricity Trade Workers Union yesterday issued the following notices:-
"With a view to strengthening the security of workers' interests, negotiations were opened following a "tai-kung" and then a strike which lasted for about 2 months and served as a warning to the management. Although the firm spirit of the entire body of comrades has not won the approval of the management during the course of these two months, yet the enthusiastic social leaders, the Chinese members, the Secretary-General and the Commissioner of Police of the Shanghai Municipal Council have learned that the comrades of our Committee were doing their utmost to preserve law and order. The comrades of our Committee have been striving for the privileges earned by the hard labour of the workers and which were granted by the firm formerly and were recognised by the Power Company in America.
"On the advice of Messrs. Doo Yueh-sun, Yu Yah-ching, Yuan Lee-tung, Zee Hsin-loh, Wong Shao-lai and others and with a view to maintaining the peace and order in the community and respecting the rights of the public, the strikers are to resume on November 22. All measures regarding the security of the workers' interests will be discussed by various Chinese members of the S.M.C. and other social leaders after the resumption of work."

The 4th District Waterworks & Electricity Trade Workers Union yesterday issued the following manifesto:-
"Fifty-four days have elapsed since the S.P.C. workers were compelled to declare a "go-slow" strike. The workers are fully aware of the importance of the electric enterprise, and therefore have attempted to secure a lawful settlement and have never resorted to illegal activities.
"Through the good offices of Messrs. Doo Yueh-sun, Yu Yah-ching, Zee Hsin-loh and other social leaders; measures regarding the resumption of work have been devised. Notwithstanding the fact that these measures are not what we expected, the efforts of the various social leaders are much appreciated."
"In order to maintain peace and order, we have accepted the advice of the mediators, and have consented to resume work this morning.
"Apart from expressing our appreciation to various public bodies and Messrs. Doo Yueh-sun, Yu Yah-ching and others, we shall maintain our original principles and serve the community."

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

上海电力公司罢工者今日复工。

第四区水电业工会“慢工”罢工委员会昨日发布如下通告：
“为了加强保障工人利益，在‘怠工’之后进行了谈判，随后发生了持续约2个月的罢工，以此警告管理层。虽然在这两个月期间，全体同仁的坚定精神未获管理层认可，但热情的社会领袖、华董、工部局总办及警务处长获悉，本委员会同仁正竭尽全力维护法律与秩序。本委员会同仁一直在争取工人们通过辛勤劳动赢得、以前由公司授予并被美国电力公司承认的特权。
“在杜月笙、虞洽庆、袁履登、奚佐洛、黄绍莱等先生的建议下，并为了维持社区的和平与秩序及尊重公众权利，罢工者将于11月22日复工。复工后，有关保障工人利益的各项措施将由工部局各位华董及其他社会领袖进行讨论。”

第四区水电业工会昨日发布如下宣言：
“上海电力公司工人被迫宣布‘慢工’罢工至今已过去五十四天。工人们充分认识到电力企业的重要性，因此一直试图寻求合法的解决方案，从未诉诸非法活动。
“通过杜月笙、虞洽庆、奚佐洛等社会领袖的斡旋；已制定出复工措施。尽管这些措施并非我们所期望的，但我们非常感激各位社会领袖的努力。”
“为了维持和平与秩序，我们接受了调解人的建议，并同意今晨复工。
“除了向各公共团体及杜月笙、虞洽庆等先生表示感谢外，我们将坚持原有原则，服务社会。”

November 22, 1933.    4    Morning Translation.

LABOUR

The General Labour Union has issued the following
circulars:-
"After the Great War, people throughout the
world became aware that war was synonymous with international
disaster and even a prosperous nation could not afford to
lose its men. In consequence, the League of Nations was
formed with the object of bringing about peace in the
world. The failure on the part of the League to suppress
war is due to lack of ability on the part of those directing
the League.
"The existence of the General Labour Union in
Shanghai is regarded as the League of the local labourers'
organizations, its aim being to protect the labourers
and to settle disputes between employers and employees,
so that both parties will co-operate and thus national
prosperity will increase. Prior to the "go-slow" strike
of the workers of the Shanghai Power Company, this Union
did its utmost to find a means to effect a reasonable
settlement of the dispute. The Union continued to work
for the welfare of society after the workers went on
a "go-slow" strike. However, no efforts could move the
management of the Power Company. As a result of the
mediation and advice of the leaders of the society, the
entire body of the Shanghai Municipality 4th District
Waterworks & Electricity Trade Workers Union are resuming
work under protest in the interests of public safety.
The resumption of work by the "go-slow" strikers can be
regarded as a 'sacrifice for public service.'
"The Union earnestly hopes that the Chinese
and foreign members of the Settlement authorities will
not allow the workers to be oppressed by the management.
Mr. Aldridge on behalf of the General Office of the
Power Company in America did issue an assurance for the
protection of the Chinese employees of the Company in
Shanghai. It is hoped that this assurance will not
become a means to cheat the employees as well as the
S.M.C.
"The Shanghai Power Company is a public
enterprise which seriously concerns the security of the
residents. The strike did not become serious owing to
the energy and good offices of our social leaders and
the preservation of good order by the strikers. In
addition to strengthening its efforts, the duties of the
Union henceforth are to protect the workers and to see
if the Chinese and foreign ratepayers of the S.M.C. and
the municipal authorities will support justice."
page_data.zh:
1933年11月22日。 4 晨间译件。

劳工事务

总工会发布了如下通告：
“大战之后，全世界人民意识到战争等同于国际灾难，即使是繁荣的国家也承受不起失去其国民的代价。因此，成立了国际联盟，旨在实现世界和平。国联未能制止战争，是由于领导国联的人士缺乏能力。
“上海总工会的存在被视为当地劳工组织的联盟，其目的是保护劳工并解决雇主与雇员之间的纠纷，以便双方合作，从而增加国家繁荣。在上海电力公司工人‘慢工’罢工之前，本会竭尽全力寻找合理解决争端的方法。在工人进行‘慢工’罢工后，本会继续为社会福利而努力。然而，任何努力都无法打动电力公司管理层。在社会领袖的调解和建议下，上海市第四区水电业工会全体出于公共安全利益的考虑，抗议性地复工。‘慢工’罢工者的复工可被视为‘为公共服务做出的牺牲’。
“本会恳切希望租界当局的华洋董事不要允许工人受到管理层的压迫。美国电力公司总办事处的阿尔德里奇（Aldridge）先生确实曾发出保证，保护公司在上海的华籍员工。希望这一保证不会成为欺骗员工以及工部局的手段。
“上海电力公司是一家严重关乎居民安全的公共企业。由于我们社会领袖的精力和斡旋，以及罢工者对良好秩序的维护，罢工并未变得严重。除了加强努力外，本会今后的职责是保护工人，并观察工部局的华洋纳税人及市政当局是否会支持正义。”

Route Army to drag the people down or will it deal with
the rebels with all the nation's might?
It is regrettable that the revolt in Fokien
should have taken place at this time when the lost
territory remains still unrecovered and the campaign to
suppress the bandits has not yet been completed. With
our undaunted spirit, we should be able to overcome all
difficulties.
After entering Fokien, the senior officers of
the 19th Route Army deported all persons who held views
opposed to theirs, employed private individuals, encroached
upon the territory of other armies and promoted their
own positions. They have now resorted to arms and
commenced a revolt and the people should turn against
them so that they will be faced with enemies on all hands
and it will be impossible for them to make any military
move. The rebels are short of funds and will not be able
to finance the new organization. Members of the Third
Party and the Social Democratic Party hold different views
and this will result in a clash, which will lead to the
break-up of the new organization.
The 19th Route Army had occupied an important
position in the history of China. We are sorry that the
Army has to-day become a tool of the Third Party and the
Social Democratic Party.
The genuine revolutionalists should have a correct
view of the whole affair and be prepared to make sacrifices
in case of necessity.

LABOUR.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

S.P.C. STRIKERS TO RESUME ON NOVEMBER 22.

With reference to the labour trouble in the
Shanghai Power Company, a settlement has been reached
through the good offices of Mr. Fessenden, Secretary-General
of the Shanghai Municipal Council, Mr. Doo Yueh-sun, member
of the Council of the Chinese Municipality, and the Chinese
members of the S.M.C.
Yesterday morning, Messrs. Fessenden, Doo Yueh-
sun and others called again at the Company to mediate.
The following measures to settle the dispute
were drawn up and passed:-
1. That the strikers be advised to resume work first.
2. That the wages of workers for the period prior to

3. That the management issue to the strikers one

政治

第十九路军是将人民拖入深渊，还是将举全国之力对付叛乱分子？
令人遗憾的是，福建的叛乱竟发生在失地尚未收复、剿匪战役尚未完成之际。凭借我们无畏的精神，我们应该能够克服一切困难。
第十九路军的高级军官进入福建后，驱逐所有持反对意见的人，任用私人，侵吞其他军队的防区，并提升他们自己的地位。他们现在诉诸武力，发动叛乱，民众应当反对他们，使他们面临四面楚歌的局面，无法进行任何军事行动。叛军资金短缺，无法为新组织提供经费。第三党和社会民主党成员持有不同观点，这将导致冲突，进而导致新组织的瓦解。
第十九路军曾在中国历史上占据重要地位。我们对该军队如今沦为第三党和社会民主党的工具感到遗憾。
真正的革命者应对整个事件有正确的看法，并在必要时准备做出牺牲。

劳工。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

上海电力公司罢工者将于11月22日复工。

关于上海电力公司的劳资纠纷，经上海公共租界工部局总办费森登（Fessenden）先生、华界市政府委员杜月笙（Doo Yueh-sun）先生以及工部局华员委员的斡旋，已达成和解。
昨天上午，费森登先生、杜月笙先生等人再次前往公司进行调解。
制定并通过了以下解决纠纷的措施：-
1. 建议罢工者先复工。
2. 罢工者复工后，全额支付罢工前期间的工人工资。
3. 管理层向罢工者发放“怠工”罢工期间一个月的工资（由杜月笙先生和工部局华员委员负责此笔款项的支付），并在罢工者复工后，由杜月笙先生和工部局华员委员就工人的其余诉求开启谈判。

LABOUR

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

LABOUR SITUATION IN THE SHANGHAI POWER COMPANY.

52 days have elapsed since the outbreak of the
"go-slow" strike trouble in the Shanghai Power Company.
Following the third intervention of Mr. Fessenden,
Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal Council, and Mr.
Doo Yueh-sun, member of the Council of the Chinese Municipa-
lity, in the S.P.C. dispute, certain measures have been
drawn up with the approval of the management. However,
many questions are awaiting settlement.
At noon yesterday, measures to effect a settlement
of the dispute were devised at a discussion between Mr. Doo
Yueh-sun and Messrs. Yuan Lee-tung, Zee Hsin-loh, Yu Yah-
ching, Chinese members of the S.M.C., Mr. Wong Shao-lai,
chairman of the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce, Loh
Ching-shih of the local Tangpu, Chu Hsueh-van, Chow Hsueh-
siang of the General Labour Union and others, These measures
will be submitted to the management to-day.
About 1,000 workers of the new and the old plants
of the Shanghai Power Company attended a meeting held at 3
p.m. yesterday by the 4th District Waterworks & Electricity
Trade Workers Union in the premises of the 1st District
Waterworks & Electricity Trade Workers Union on Kuo Fo Road,
Nantao. Loh Ching-shih of the local Tangpu and Chu Hsueh-
van of the General Labour Union were also present to give
advice during the function.
It was resolved that the measures devised by
Messrs. Fessenden, Doo Yueh-sun and others be accepted, and
that the workers should calmly await the final settlement.

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

上海电力公司的劳工局势。

上海电力公司“怠工”罢工纠纷爆发至今已过去52天。继上海公共租界工部局总办费森登先生和华界市政府委员杜月笙先生第三次介入上海电力公司纠纷后，已在管理层批准下制定了一些措施。然而，许多问题尚待解决。
昨天中午，杜月笙先生与工部局华员委员袁履登（Yuan Lee-tung）、席德懋（Zee Hsin-loh）、虞洽卿（Yu Yah-ching）先生，上海华人商会主席王筱籁（Wong Shao-lai）先生，本地唐浦（音译）的陆京士（Loh Ching-shih），以及总工会的朱学范（Chu Hsueh-van）、周雪祥（Chow Hsueh-siang）等人进行讨论， devised 了解决纠纷的措施。这些措施将于今日提交给管理层。
上海电力公司新老厂房的约1000名工人参加了昨天下午3点由第四区水电业职工公会在南市国福路第一区水电业职工公会会所举行的会议。本地唐浦（音译）的陆京士和总工会的朱学范也出席了活动并提供建议。
会议决定接受费森登先生、杜月笙先生等人制定的措施，工人们应冷静等待最终解决方案。

Shanghai Power Company - Situation

The situation in the various departments of the
Shanghai Power Company remains unchanged this morning.

At 1.30 p.m. November 19, Tu Yueh-sung entertained
representatives of the Chinese members of the S.M.C., the
General Labour Union and the strikers of the Shanghai

that the public would not suffer any inconvenience. The
meeting then agreed to ask the management of the Shanghai
Power Company to make the advance of a month's pay to be
given to employees when work is resumed; a gratuity which
need not be paid back, and that negotiations in this sense
be conducted by the Chinese members of the S.M.C. with the

advance. The meeting decided that the sixty men, whose
services are to be terminated, should be permitted to
resign and draw in full all pay and gratuities due to them.

November 19, 1933. Morning Translation 19/11/33.

LABOUR

Min Pao and other local newspapers :

LABOUR SITUATION IN THE SHANGHAI POWER COMPANY.

With reference to the "go-slow" strike of the workers of the Shanghai Power Company, Mr. Stirling Fessenden, Secretary-General of the S.M.C. and Mr. Doo Yue Sung, member of the Assembly of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, formally mediated with the Shanghai Power Co. The situation remains unsettled owing to the views of the company on certain points.
Today Mr. Doo Yue Sung will hold a meeting with Chinese members of the S.M.C. in the premises of the Chinese Bankers Association at which measures to deal with the matter will be discussed.
The 4th District Water and Electricity Workers Union decided to hold a general meeting of the entire body of its members at 3 p.m. today at the Nantao 1st District Water and Electricity Workers Union to devise final methods concerning the dispute and has requested the local Tangpu and the General Labour Union to deal members to attend the meeting.

Chen Pao and other local newspapers :

WORKERS OF THE B.A.T. FACTORIES

In connection with the labour dispute in the B.A.T. factories, which followed as the result of the refusal to amend the agreement between the management and the workers, yesterday the workers union submitted petitions to the local Tangpu and other political organs.
Mr. O.K. Yui, Chief Secretary of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, promised to instruct the management to amend the agreement and advised the workers not to resort to unlawful activities.

Chen Pao and other local newspapers :

STRIKE OF LOCAL DYERS

Following the declaration of the "go-slow" strike of the local dyers, the Bureau of Social Affairs has had already held a meeting but the workers have not resumed work as the managements have not yet completed the guarantee agreement for the issue of gratuities to the workers.
Yesterday a meeting was held at which it was resolved to detail Pan Kar Min (潘家敏) to negotiate with the workers over the question of resuming work and should the workers not resumed on November 20, the Dyeing Shop Owners Association will request the authorities to adopt necessary action and will refuse to accept any other proposals.

英美烟厂工人

Labour

Shanghai Power Company - Situation

The situation in the various departments of the
Shanghai Power Company remains unchanged this morning.

Slight uneasiness is noticed among the men at
Riverside Power Station as the result of the partial
breakdown in the negotiations for settlement, there is,
however, nothing to indicate that the men, who have so
far remained loyal, intend to leave their work or cause
trouble.

At 11.20 a.m. November 17, three representatives of
the Strike Committee called at Tu Yueh-sung's home, 216
Rue Wagner, and endeavoured to persuade him to resume
negotiations with the Shanghai Power Company on behalf
of the strikers. This request was rejected by Tu who
explained that he could do nothing further in the matter.
The representatives then asked if he would grant a
further loan to carry on the strike, but this was also
refused.

B.C.C. Footung Factories - Unrest among workers

The workers of the B.C.C. Footung Factories are
agitating against the prohibition of the collection of
union fees on the factory premises by the management.
The Bureau of Social Affairs and local Kuomintang Headquarters
were approached on the subject by four representatives of
the 5th District (Footung) Tobacco Factory Workers' Union
on November 17 and were informed that the matter would
be investigated.

LABOUR

LABOUR SITUATION IN THE SHANGHAI POWER COMPANY.

At 11 a.m. yesterday Mr. Stirling Fessenden,
Secretary-General of the S.M.C., and Mr. Doo Yueh Sung,
member of the Assembly of the Municipality of Greater

The management submitted certain proposals to
affect a settlement.
It was arranged yesterday that further negotiations
would be held on the morning of November 16 at the same
place as Mr. Doo would solicit the views of the labourers
concerning the proposals of the Power Company.
The "go-slow" strikers have agreed to accept
the intervention of the mediators and are quietly awaiting
the settlement of the dispute. means
It is believed that a of settling the
dispute may be obtained during to-day's discussions.

"The labour situation in the Shanghai Power
Company is still unchanged to-day. The "go-slow" strikers

deserve admiration. Mr. Fessenden and Mr. Doo are
formally mediating in the dispute and the case is proceeding
favourably."

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

STRIKE OF LOCAL DYERS.

With reference to the strike of local dyers,
the Bureau of Social Affairs held a meeting yesterday of
representatives of the employers and employees.
The following three measures to settle the
dispute were devised:-
1) That fees be issued by silk and cloth dyeing
works to workers in accordance with the list of the fees
drawn up in 1927 by the former Bureau of Agriculture,
Labour and Commerce.
2) That deputies of the Dyeing Workers Union
visit dyeing works and collect the fees between the 5th
day and the 9th day of each month, and that the money
immediately distributed among the workers.

本地染匠罢工。

关于本地染匠罢工一事，社会局昨日召开了雇主和雇员代表的会议。
制定了以下三项解决纠纷的措施：
1) 丝绸和布料染色厂应按照前农工商局于1927年编制的费用清单向工人发放费用。

LABOUR

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

THE LABOUR SITUATION IN THE SHANGHAI POWER COMPANY

At 11 a.m. yesterday Mr. Stirling Fessenden,
Secretary-General of the S.M.C., and Mr. Doo Yue Sung,
member of the Assembly of the Municipality of Greater
Shanghai, accompanied by Tsai Foo Daung (蔡福棠),

the visitors and the question was discussed for over two
hours. Certain decisions were reached.

be held to-day. There is a hope that the dispute will
be settled.

LABOUR.

- Chen Pao and other local newspapers

D5210

LABOUR SITUATION IN THE SHANGHAI POWER COMPANY.

Regarding the labour trouble in the Shanghai
Power Company, Mr. Fessenden, Secretary-General of the
Shanghai Municipal Council, and Mr. Doo Yueh-sun, member
of the Council of the Chinese Municipality, are submitting
proposals with a view to settling the dispute.
The Company carried out its programme
of attempting to engage new hands, but only a few persons
have applied for registration and even these will be of
no use owing to lack of technical skill. Therefore, the
Company yesterday ceased to employ new hands.
In an interview yesterday with our reporter,
a certain distribution worker of the new plant of the
Shanghai Power Company stated that the labour trouble
had remained unsettled for more than one month. The
management is still insincere despite the concessions
offered by the workers. It has been resolved to calmly
await the settlement of the dispute and should the
forthcoming mediations end in a deadlock, the distribution
workers would voluntarily join the "go-slow" strike.

关于上海电力公司的劳资纠纷，上海工部局秘书长费森登先生（Mr. Fessenden）和华界市议会成员杜月笙先生正在提交提案，以期解决纠纷。
公司执行了试图招募新员工的计划，但只有少数人申请登记，而且由于缺乏技术技能，这些人也无济于事。因此，公司昨天停止雇用新员工。
上海电力公司新厂的一名配电工人在昨天接受本报记者采访时称，劳资纠纷已悬而未决一个多月。尽管工人做出了让步，但资方仍然缺乏诚意。已决定冷静等待纠纷解决，如果即将进行的调解陷入僵局，配电工人将自愿参加“怠工”罢工。

Labour

D 5310 Shanghai Power Company - Situation

The situation in the various departments of the
Shanghai Power Company remains unchanged this morning,
November 9.

Of the 300 men who presented themselves at Riverside
Power Station on November 8, seeking employment, 24
were examined and told to return later.

At 11.30 a.m. November 8, while a male Chinese was
returning along Pingliang Road, after having applied at
the Riverside Station for employment, he was set upon
and assaulted by three men. Police arrived on the scene
and succeeded in effecting the arrest of one of the
assailants who proved to be an ex-employee of the
Shanghai Power Company. He has been charged with
intimidation and will appear before Court to-day, November 9.

S
At 1.30 p.m. November 8, two delegates of the Shanghai
Power Company Workers' Strike Committee Chu Hsueh-fan
(朱学范) and Chow Hsueh-siang (周学湘), committee members
of the General Labour Union, at the Chinese Young Men's
Lecturing Group building, Small West Gate, City, and asked
assistance in securing the release of a striker who was
arrested that day by the Yangtsepoo Police Station.
Chu Hsueh-fan and Chow Hsueh-siang promised to comply with
their request.

It is learned that the fines imposed by the Court on
the three men charged with intimidation on November 7
were paid by the Strike Committee of the 4th District Water
& Electricity Workers' Union, and that the committee will
hold themselves responsible for the payment of any fines
imposed on strikers for acts of intimidation.

劳工

D 5310 上海电力公司 - 局势

今晨（11月9日），上海电力公司各部门的局势保持不变。

11月8日，有300人前往江边发电厂求职，其中24人接受了审查，并被告知稍后返回。

11月8日上午11时30分，一名中国男子在江边电站求职后沿平凉路返回时，遭到三名男子的袭击和殴打。警察赶到现场，成功逮捕了一名袭击者，经查实其为上海电力公司的前雇员。他被控恐吓罪，将于今天（11月9日）出庭。

S
11月8日下午1时30分，上海电力公司工人罢工委员会的两名代表、总工会委员朱学范和周学湘，在市小西门中华青年会演讲厅大楼，请求协助释放当天被杨树浦警察局逮捕的一名罢工者。朱学范和周学湘答应满足他们的请求。

据悉，11月7日因恐吓罪被起诉的三人所受的法院罚款，已由第四区水电工会罢工委员会支付，并且该委员会将负责支付罢工者因恐吓行为而被判处的任何罚款。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 17, 1933

POWER CO. STANDS
FIRM ON STRIKE
Mediation With S.M.C.
Or Chinese Denied;
Men May Return

Officials of the Shanghai Power Company yesterday denied that they had ever entered into negotiations concerning the ending of the “strike” being carried on by some of their employees.

The vernacular press has stated recently that certain Chinese officials had conferred with representatives of the S.M.C. over the strike, and that negotiations were being attempted.

In answer to an inquiry yesterday, officials of the Power Company stated that they had told the S.M.C. representatives that, if any men were to apply for positions, they would be given preference for available jobs, and that if they needed money to tide them over until pay day, the Company would arrange advances. The latter has often been done in the past, it was said.

However, it was insisted that the Company was standing firm on its attitude of no negotiation and no compromise with the strikers. As a matter of fact it may be remembered that the Company some time ago in a notice virtually told the non-working employees that, if they did not take up their duties by a certain date, their jobs would be opened to applicants. That date passed and about 300 new employees were investigated preliminary to hiring them, so it is evident that the Company considers the walkout a thing of the past.

A number of Chinese reports yesterday had it that the strikers were planning to re-enter the stations and go to work on Monday. The reports could not be confirmed.

《字林西报》，1933年11月17日，星期五

电力公司在罢工问题上立场坚定
否认与工部局或中方进行调解；
工人可能复工

上海电力公司官员昨天否认他们曾就结束部分员工正在进行的“罢工”进行过谈判。

中文报纸最近称，某些中国官员已与工部局代表就罢工问题进行了会谈，并正在尝试谈判。

在回答昨天的询问时，电力公司官员表示，他们已告诉工部局代表，如果有人申请职位，将在现有职位中优先考虑他们，如果他们需要在发薪日前借钱度日，公司将安排预支款项。据说，过去经常这样做。

然而，他们坚持认为，公司在不与罢工者谈判和不妥协的态度上立场坚定。事实上，人们可能还记得，公司不久前在一份通知中实际上告诉未上班的员工，如果他们在某个日期前不履行职责，他们的工作岗位将对申请人开放。该日期已过，约300名新员工在接受初步调查以备录用，因此显然公司认为这次停工已成为过去。

昨天有多份中文报道称，罢工者计划于周一重返电站上班。这些报道未能得到证实。

INTIMIDATION MOVE
BY STRIKERS

Power Co. Incidents; No
Violence Is Used; One
"Suspect Released

Following the decision on Fri-
day of the striking employees of
the Shanghai Power Company to
punish severely any worker who
answered the company's call for
new hands, two cases of intimida-
tion were reported yesterday. It
is understood that no physical
violence was used.

The strikers' system was to
watch from a distance those who
presented themselves at the com-
pany's works in answer to the
notice that new hands would be
engaged and that old employees
would be given preference, and
thus ascertain those whom they
consider traitors.

Yesterday morning a number of
strikers called on one of the men
in the Kashing Road district who
had offered himself for work and,
without using violence or making
direct threats, gave him to under-
stand, it is believed, that it would
not be wholesome for him to work
for the Power Company. Three
Chinese were subsequently arrest-
ed in connection with the incident.
Following a similar happening in
the Yangtzepoo district one man
was arrested.

It could not be ascertained late
yesterday whether it was intended
to prefer any charge against the
three arrested at Kashing Road;
but the Yangtzepoo suspect was

罢工者的恐吓举动

电力公司事件；未使用暴力；一名“嫌疑人”获释

继周五上海电力公司罢工员工决定严惩任何响应公司招募新员工号召的工人之后，昨日报告了两起恐吓案件。据悉，期间未发生肢体暴力。

罢工者的做法是远距离监视那些根据公司发布的将雇佣新员工且优先考虑老员工的通知而前往公司工厂求职的人，从而查明他们眼中的叛徒。

昨日上午，数名罢工者拜访了嘉善路地区一名主动求职的男子，据信在未使用暴力或直接威胁的情况下，让他明白为电力公司工作对他没有好处。随后有三名华人因此事被捕。在杨树浦地区发生类似事件后，有一人被捕。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 4, 1933

Power Company Notice Gets
300 Requests For Jobs

Strikers Hold Mass Meeting, Choose Quartette
To Appeal To Nanking Authorities; All
Employees Now Back At Cigarette Co.

Approximately 300 Chinese men appeared yesterday at the Fearon Road and Riverside stations of the Shanghai Power Company in answer to a Company notice that the striking employees either appear for work or consider themselves dismissed.
However, a great many of the 300 Chinese were persons who had never been employed at the Company. The names of all were taken for examination and reference, and they were told to return on Tuesday.

Tobacco Strike Ended
The other big strike in Settlement labour circles, that of the Thorburn Road plant of the British Cigarette Company, was announced as having come to an end. About 80 per cent. of the plant's 3,000 employees returned to their positions on Thursday, which allowed the plant to resume production. Yesterday the remaining 20 per cent. came into the factory and resumed work unconditionally. The Chinese press asserts that the workers came back to the factory on the orders of the Fourth District Rolled Tobacco Workers' Union and of the Tangpu, both of which have sent a petition to the Municipality authorities requesting assistance.

Power Strikers Meet
Because of the "ultimatum" notice posted by the Power Company on Wednesday, the Fourth District Waterworks and Electricity Workers' Union called a general meeting of the Power Company strikers for yesterday morning. The assembly took place at the Kung Wu Theatre, West Gate. Approximately 1,500 strikers attended the meeting, the vernacular press declared yesterday and they passed three resolutions in connection with their walkout. The resolutions were as follows:

Appeal To Nanking
That the strike should be continued and members of the Union swear not to resume work until their aims are obtained: that representatives be sent to appeal before the Central Kuomintang Headquarters at Nanking, the Central Government, and the Ministries of Labour and Industries: that strict punishment be awarded to persons betraying the strikers.
Messrs. Chu Hou-sen, Chiang Chi-min, Chen Yu-fah, and Tsao Teh-chuan were elected as representatives to make the trip to Nanking and present the appeal.
The meeting was conducted quietly and there was little need for the squad of police from the Bureau of Public Safety which was sent there as a precaution.

电力公司通知收到300份求职申请

罢工者举行群众大会，选出四人代表团向南京当局请愿；卷烟厂所有员工现已复工

昨日，约300名中国男子出现在上海电力公司的斐伦路（Fearon Road）和江边站，以回应公司发布的通知，即罢工员工要么返岗工作，要么视为被解雇。
然而，这300名中国人中有许多人是从未被该公司雇佣过的人员。所有人的姓名均被登记以备审查和参考，并被告知于周二返回。

烟草罢工结束
租界劳工界的另一次大罢工，即英商烟草公司韬朋路（Thorburn Road）工厂的罢工，宣布已结束。该厂3000名员工中约有80%于周四返岗，使得工厂得以恢复生产。昨日，剩余的20%也进入工厂并无条件复工。中文报刊声称，工人们是遵照第四区卷烟工人公会和汤朴（Tangpu，音译）的命令返回工厂的，这两者均已向市政当局提交请愿书请求协助。

电力罢工者集会
由于电力公司于周三张贴了“最后通牒”通知，第四区水电工人公会于昨日上午召开了电力公司罢工者全体大会。据昨日白话文报刊称，集会在西门公舞大戏院（Kung Wu Theatre）举行。约1500名罢工者参加了大会，并通过了三项关于此次罢工的决议。决议如下：

会议进行得平静有序，作为预防措施派往那里的公安局警队几乎无需发挥作用。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, November 3, 1933

Power Strikers
In Massmeeting

Pass Three Resolutions
Pledging To Remain
Off Their Jobs

Approximately 1500 striking employees of the Shanghai Power Company this morning packed the Kungho (Republican) Theatre at Fangpangchiao, West Gate, and held their first general meeting since the declaration of the walk-out more than a month ago.

Three resolutions were passed voicing their "determination to fight to the end." The resolutions were:
That the strike should be continued and members of the labor union swear not to resume work until their aims are attained;
That during the strike, strict punishment should be given for those who betray the cause of the union and who cause disturbances under instigation of third parties;
and
That representatives be sent to appeal to the Central Kuomintang Headquarters, National Government, Executive Yuan and Ministry of Industries.

Representatives Elected
Messrs. Chu Hou-sen, Chiang Chi-min, Chen Yu-fah, and Tsao Teh-chuan were elected representatives for the trip to Nanking to present the strikers' case before the authorities and to seek for support from the official circles.

The meeting was started at 9 o'clock this morning under the presidium of five leaders. Mr. Loh King-ss, of the City Kuomintang, and Mr. Chu Yueh-fan, of the General Labor Union, attended. With a squad of armed police from the Bureau of Public Safety standing by and group of strikers' pickets guarding the iron grills, the strikers discussed the resolutions with the house packed.

Result Of Company Move
The meeting was called as result of the company's announcement that loyal workers will be taken back and strikers will be officially discharged and their jobs replaced by new employees. The union is understood to have been alarmed by the company's action in mobilizing a skeleton staff sufficient to carry on the electric supply.

The strikers declared in a manifesto issued yesterday that the company is sending trucks "in four directions" to force employees to re-enter the plant in order to break the strike. They blamed the company for its alleged adamant policy in refusing a settlement and announced their intention to fight to the "bitter end."

Supply Not Impaired
The situation at the power company's plants remain unchanged with the supply unimpaired.
It is understood that the company is not pressing the early employment of replacements of loyal workers whose return apparently is imminent from the radical elements.
A majority of the B.O.C. strikers were reported back at work and the Thompson Street picket tie-up was believed at an end.

noted
Ben Golan
6/4/33.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1933年11月3日，星期五

电力罢工者
举行群众大会

通过三项决议
承诺继续停工

今日上午，约1500名上海电力公司罢工员工挤满了西门方浜桥的共和大戏院（Kungho (Republican) Theatre），举行了自一个多月前宣布罢工以来的首次全体大会。

大会通过了三项表达其“战斗到底决心”的决议。决议内容为：
罢工应继续进行，工会成员宣誓在目标达成前不复工；
在罢工期间，严厉惩罚那些背叛工会事业以及在第三方煽动下制造混乱的人；
以及
派遣代表向中国国民党中央党部、国民政府、行政院和实业部请愿。

选举代表
朱厚森（Chu Hou-sen，音译）、蒋志敏（Chiang Chi-min，音译）、陈玉发（Chen Yu-fah，音译）和曹德全（Tsao Teh-chuan，音译）先生当选为代表，前往南京向当局陈述罢工者的情况，并寻求官方阶层的支持。

会议由五位领导人组成的主席团主持，于今早9点开始。市国民党部的罗金司（Loh King-ss，音译）先生和总工会的朱月凡（Chu Yueh-fan，音译）先生出席了会议。在公安局武装警队在一旁待命以及一组罢工纠察队守卫铁栅栏的情况下，罢工者在座无虚席的会场中讨论了各项决议。

公司举动的结果

召开此次会议是由于公司宣布将重新录用忠诚工人，正式解雇罢工者并由新员工接替其职位。据悉，工会对公司动员足以维持电力供应的骨干人员这一举动感到惊慌。

罢工者在昨日发表的宣言中声称，公司正派出卡车“四处”强迫员工重返工厂以破坏罢工。他们指责公司拒绝和解的所谓强硬政策，并宣布打算“战斗到底”。

供应未受影响

电力公司各厂的情况保持不变，供应未受影响。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 3. 1933
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL C. & S. B. R. No. D
Date /

Strikers Of Power Company
Must Decide To-day

Company Posts Ultimatum; To Open Gates This
Morning; Majority Of B C. C. Employees
Return To Positions Yesterday

A crisis looms this morning for the 1,400 striking workers of the Shanghai Power Company. On Wednesday the Company posted notices that the gates to the Fearon Road and Riverside Station plants would be opened at the usual working time, and that strikers who returned could obtain positions.

The "catch" for the strikers is that if they don't put in an appearance, their jobs will be given to someone else, which will put them in the position of striking from jobs that they haven't got.

It is the Company's contention that the workers have been under the influence of agitators, and that they have been prevented from returning to work because of coercive efforts of union leaders. "Underground" reports would seem to bear out this contention, as several strikers returned to work last week and many more were said to have turned against their leaders and to be thinking favourably of returning.

The action of the agitators and union leaders in attempting to intimidate the workers by bombs and assaults, and, in one extreme case, shooting, led to considerable adverse thought on the part of the strikers and a large portion of the Chinese populace not connected with the strike.

Decisive Action To-day

The next step in the strike is up to the workers. If a large number wish to return, as is anticipated, the strike leaders will have great difficulty in stopping them. The ultimatum of the Company may prove to be the incentive necessary to overcome the fear entertained by the strikers of the leaders.

The strike at the Thorburn Road plant of the British Cigarette Company came to an abrupt end, at least temporarily, yesterday morning when some 80 per cent. of the strikers returned to their jobs.

The end of the walkout came as a result of orders from the local office of the Tangpu, it is said. The vernacular press has asserted the mediation in the affair has been referred by the Social Bureau to the Municipality authorities following two unsuccessful attempts by the Bureau to hold mediation meetings. Early in the strike, the management of the tobacco plant refused an offer by the Bureau to mediate, and declared that it would carry on its own negotiations.

Agitators Cause Strikes

This strike, as in the walkout at the Power Company, has been caused by a small minority of union leaders and agitators, it has been reported.

Whether or not the tobacco company management has formed an agreement with its workers could not be ascertained yesterday, but the machines of the Thorburn Road were running yesterday and enough of the 2,000 employees were in attendance to assure operation of the plant.

上海工部局 C. & S. B. R. D 号

电力公司罢工者
必须今日做出决定

公司张贴最后通牒；今晨开放大门；大部分英商烟草公司员工昨日返岗

对于上海电力公司的1400名罢工工人来说，今晨危机迫在眉睫。周三，公司张贴通知称，斐伦路和江边站工厂的大门将在正常工作时间开放，返回的罢工者可以获得职位。

给罢工者设下的“圈套”是，如果他们不露面，他们的工作将交给其他人，这将使他们处于对尚未拥有的工作进行罢工的地位。

公司认为，工人一直受到煽动者的影响，并且由于工会领导人的胁迫努力而被阻止返回工作岗位。“地下”消息似乎证实了这一观点，因为上周有几名罢工者返回工作岗位，据说还有更多人转而反对他们的领导人，并倾向于返回。

煽动者和工会领导人试图通过炸弹和袭击，甚至在一个极端案例中通过枪击来恐吓工人，这在罢工者以及与罢工无关的大部分中国民众中引起了相当大的反感。

今日的决定性行动

罢工的下一步取决于工人。如果像预期的那样有大量工人希望返回，罢工领导者将很难阻止他们。公司的最后通牒可能会成为克服罢工者对领导者恐惧所需的激励因素。

英商烟草公司韬朋路工厂的罢工于昨日上午突然结束，至少是暂时性的，当时约80%的罢工者返回了工作岗位。

据说，罢工的结束是由于汤朴（Tangpu，音译）当地办事处下达命令的结果。白话文报刊声称，在社会局两次尝试举行调解会议未果后，此事的调解已移交市政当局。在罢工初期，烟草厂管理层拒绝了社会局的调解提议，并声明将进行自行谈判。

煽动者引发罢工

据报道，这次罢工，如同电力公司的罢工一样，是由少数工会领导人和煽动者引起的。

昨日无法确定烟草公司管理层是否与其工人达成了协议，但韬朋路的机器昨日正在运转，2000名员工中有足够多的人出勤以确保工厂运营。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 1, 1933

THE LOCAL LABOUR
SITUATION

In spite of incidents of intimidation in various parts of Greater Shanghai, the number of workers who returned to their places yesterday for a second time at the Shanghai Power Co., did not diminish. It will be recalled that the strike is now of more than one month's duration. At least four cases of intimidation and attempted violence were reported yesterday.

The return on Monday of workers for the first time was reported in several Chinese newspapers as follows:—"At 5 a.m., yesterday (October 30), some ten senior staff employees of the Power Co., including foreign and Chinese engineers, accompanied by detectives and constables (Municipal police) ......... pulled 'go—slow' strikers into nine motorcars and by force conveyed them to the Plant. Some 30 workers were thus forced to enter the Plant."

Also at the B.C.C., the general attitude of employees is to return to their places and it would appear as though the back of the strike is broken. Interdepartmental relations among personnel are said to handicap resumption.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, October 25, 1933
7006

Power Difficulty
Deemed Near End

Progress Made, Belief,
As Result Of New
Deliberations

Prospects were seen today for an early settlement of the labor dispute at the Shanghai Power Company as result of deliberations by both the Shanghai Municipal Council and the local Chinese authorities during the last few days. Assisted by Mr. Pao Kuo-hua, chief of the labor department of the Ministry of Industries, the Bureau of Social Affairs of the City Government of Greater Shanghai is said to be progressing in its efforts to settle the strike. A written report summarizing their findings is expected to be submitted to the bureau this afternoon ready to make clear and definite, for the first time since the declaration of the walkout 27 days ago, the employers' case.

Matters In Hand

The report is expected to be finished which, it is understood, contemplates the holding of a mediation conference at the Bureau's offices in Nantao one of the measures for a settlement of the strike. The mediation conference, if held, will be attended by representatives of the Power Company and the striking employees of the company. It will be presided and attended by officials of the Bureau, and probably Mr. Pao of the Ministry of Industries.

The City Kuomintang Headquarters here is also understood to be acting for a settlement of the strike. Investigations are known to have been launched by the tang-pu to prevent radical elements from controlling the labor union.

S. M. C. Moves In

The Shanghai Municipal Council is now reported to have acted to settle the labor dispute. Chinese reports state that Mr. Tu Yueh-sen, prominent and influential local merchant, has been requested by the city body to help in settling the strike. Mr. Tu is said to have conferred with Mr. Stirling Fessenden, S.M.C. secretary-general, yesterday afternoon.

As a member of the Provisional City Council of Greater Shanghai, Mr. Tu has on his record many successes as a mediator of local labor disputes. It is expected that his services will eventually help the local authorities in attaining a settlement of the power company strike.

Meeting Today Scheduled

The local General Labor Union was to hold a meeting of representatives of various local labor unions at its Nantao offices at 3 o'clock this afternoon. Ostensibly the General Labor Union called the meeting to discuss the Power Company strike and the meeting this afternoon was called to take up exploratory steps regarding alleged grievances against the company.

The Shanghai Electric Works Association have delivered a letter to the Power Company yesterday asking that an early settlement be arranged in order that their business will not be affected. Owing to shortage of funds at the company, many of their installment payments had been delayed, they stated.

处理中的事项

据悉，该报告即将完成，其中考虑在社会局南市办事处举行调解会议，作为解决罢工的措施之一。如果举行调解会议，电力公司代表和公司罢工员工代表将出席。会议由社会局官员主持并出席，实业部的鲍先生也可能出席。

据了解，本市国民党市党部也在为罢工和解而行动。已知党部已展开调查，以防止激进分子控制工会。

工部局采取行动

据报道，上海公共租界工部局现已采取行动解决劳资纠纷。中文报道称，本市机构已请求当地著名且有影响力的商人杜月笙先生帮助解决罢工。据说杜先生昨日下午与工部局总办费信惇先生进行了会谈。

作为大上海临时市议会的成员，杜先生在调解本地劳资纠纷方面有许多成功记录。预计他的服务最终将帮助地方当局达成解决电力公司罢工的协议。

定于今日开会

本地总工会定于今天下午3点在其南市办事处召开各地方工会代表会议。表面上，总工会召集会议是为了讨论电力公司罢工，今天下午的会议旨在就针对公司的所谓不满采取初步步骤。

上海电气同业公会昨日致函电力公司，要求尽早安排和解，以免其业务受到影响。他们表示，由于公司资金短缺，许多分期付款已被推迟。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, October 24, 1933

Strikers' Demands
Sought Officially

Envoy Of Nanking Calls
Trio To Explain
Power Trouble

Officials of the Ministry of Industries Bureau of Social Affairs of the City Government of Greater Shanghai and City Kuomintang Headquarters, today deliberated in an effort to find effective measures for the settlement of the Shanghai Power Company strike which entered its twenty-sixth day today.

Mr. Pao Kuo-hua, chief of the labor department of the ministry, arrived from Nanking recently to obtain first-hand information regarding the strike and to help the local authorities to find a measure for the settlement. Following several conferences Mr. Pao yesterday afternoon summoned three representatives from the striking ex-employees for a detailed and definite report.

In the presence of Mr. Wong Kang of the Social Affairs Bureau, and Mr. Loh Ying-tau of the city taxepu. Mr. Pao asked the representatives to explain their case and their demands in the present strike. The representatives were Yang Zao-kan, Chen Yu-fa and Ting Ping-sung.

Following a lengthy conference, Mr. Pao instructed the strikers' representatives to submit a written report setting forth a set of their demands and their reasons. This report must be submitted in a period of three days in order that actions may be immediately taken by the officials to study into the measures for the settlement of the strike, Mr. Pao told the representatives.

Chinese reports indicate that upon receipt of the report from the strikers' union, an attempt will be made by Mr. Pao to arrange a joint conference between the two parties to settle the strike.

It was also reported that Hung-ten another representative of the striking Power Company employees, was summoned by the Shanghai Municipal Council to give their case.

南京特使召见
三人解释
电力纠纷

大上海市政府社会局、实业部官员及市国民党党部今日进行商议，努力寻找有效措施以解决已进入第二十六天的上海电力公司罢工。

实业部劳工局局长鲍国华先生近期从南京抵达，以获取关于罢工的第一手资料，并帮助地方当局找到解决措施。经过几次会议后，鲍先生昨日下午召见了三名前雇员罢工代表，要求他们提供详细且明确的报告。

在社会局王康先生和市党部罗英陶先生在场的情况下，鲍先生要求代表们解释他们在本次罢工中的案情和诉求。代表分别为杨造干（音译）、陈玉发（音译）和丁平松（音译）。

经过长时间的会议，鲍先生指示罢工代表提交一份书面报告，列明他们的诉求及理由。鲍先生告诉代表们，这份报告必须在三天内提交，以便官员们立即采取行动研究解决罢工的措施。

中文报道指出，收到罢工工会的报告后，鲍先生将尝试安排双方举行联合会议以解决罢工。

另有报道称，上海电力公司罢工员工的另一名代表洪登（音译）被上海公共租界工部局召见，以陈述其案情。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, October 23, 1933
7484

Do the Strikers
Have a Case?

DO the Shanghai Power Company's striking ex-employees have any definite quarrel with the company which can stand the light of public statement?
If they do, The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury hereby offers them full and free use of its columns to state their grievances, and guarantees them full protection against being victimized because of their willingness to take responsibility for making the statements.
If they do not, it is clear that the statements of the company must be taken at their full face value and that the growing public conviction that the strikers as well as the company are being victimized by their leaders is fully justified.

THE offer of full publicity for any grievance any bona-fide ex-employee of the company wishes to state as his reason for joining the strikers is made by this newspaper in a final effort to obtain a clear and correct statement of the strikers' side of the dispute.
Thus far, our efforts to obtain a clear and concise statement of what, exactly, the employees hope to gain by the strike have resulted in utter failure. The Shanghai Power Company tells us that the reason for this result is that the workers have no grievances which can be stated openly and frankly, and that the company itself is unable to discover a basis for the strike other than the desire of union organisers to show their power.

THERE have been, it is true, numerous veiled charges against the company made in the Chinese and foreign press; but thus far no statement has been made which gives definite reasons for the cessation of work.
The regular newspapers have been called out whole sale by anonymous attacks upon the company, but these attacks have been so vague and general that it has been impossible to determine what specific grievances the strikers have. It has been claimed that the workers are being forced to strike by union organisers, and that the company is willing to meet any legitimate demands. The company states that it has offered to arbitrate all disputes, but that the union leaders have refused to accept this offer. The company also states that it has offered to increase wages, but that the union leaders have refused to accept this offer. The company further states that it has offered to improve working conditions, but that the union leaders have refused to accept this offer. The company finally states that it has offered to recognize the union, but that the union leaders have refused to accept this offer.

Here are the terms of this newspaper's offer, in an effort to fully air the causes of the walk-out. The matter is a public one. Already violence has been done. The company has offered $5000 for the arrest and conviction of the persons who attacked and nearly killed a company worker who refused to go on strike. Matters cannot be permitted to reach a more serious state. Here are the terms of this newspaper's offer to the striking employees:
1. Any bona-fide ex-employee of the Shanghai Power Company now on strike may come in person to the offices of the newspaper at 21 Avenue Edward VII, and present his charges against the company either orally and/or in writing, either in English or Chinese, to the editor of the newspaper, T. O. Thackrey, together with whatever proofs may exist regarding the truth of the charges. Use of the employee's name must be permitted in the interests of good faith.
2. The editor guarantees that charges made by such an employee and in such a manner will be fully printed, and that an answer to the charges will be demanded both privately and publicly from the company, and that if the company has no answer or refuses to answer that this fact will also be published clearly and fully.
3. The newspaper will NOT print any anonymous attacks either upon the strikers or upon the company, nor will it heed unsigned statements sent rather than brought to the newspaper offices. The newspaper will NOT accept "third party" statements as being legitimate. That is, charges must be made by the striker or strikers themselves, and in person, and the ex-employee must be willing to reveal his name and former position.
4. Charges against the company must be confined to charges having to do with the reason for the employee's having struck work; that is, general charges of mismanagement without specific cases will not be entertained.
5. The columns of the newspaper will be held open to any ex-employee on strike until noon Saturday October 28, by which time it is considered ample time will have been allowed for the visit of any employee to the offices of the newspaper to state his case.
6. Full protection against discrimination by the company against any employee making public his grievances will be afforded by the newspaper, in the event that the workers' charges are found to be true, or if it is found that the worker himself has been duped into believing them true.
7. If the company is ready to meet any or all of the demands of the strikers, the newspaper will publish this fact, and will urge the strikers to return to work. If the company is not ready to meet any of the demands of the strikers, the newspaper will publish this fact, and will urge the strikers to continue their strike. The newspaper will also publish any statement made by the company regarding the strike, and will urge the strikers to consider this statement carefully before taking any further action. The newspaper will also publish any statement made by the union leaders regarding the strike, and will urge the strikers to consider this statement carefully before taking any further action. The newspaper will also publish any statement made by any other party regarding the strike, and will urge the strikers to consider this statement carefully before taking any further action. The newspaper will also publish any statement made by any other party regarding the strike, and will urge the strikers to consider this statement carefully before taking any further action.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1933年10月23日，星期一
7484

罢工者
有理吗？

上海电力公司罢工的离职员工与公司之间是否存在任何经得起公开声明检验的明确纠纷？
如果存在，《上海晚邮报与信使报》特此向他们提供本报名专栏的全部及免费使用权，以陈述其不满，并保证他们不会因愿意承担责任发表声明而遭受迫害。
如果不存在，那么显然必须完全采信公司的声明，且公众日益坚信罢工者与公司均受其领导层之害的观点是完全正当的。

本报提出让任何真诚的前员工充分公开其加入罢工队伍的理由所引发的任何不满，旨在最终努力获取关于罢工方立场的清晰且正确的陈述。
迄今为止，我们试图获取一份清晰简明的声明，说明员工究竟希望通过罢工获得什么，但结果彻底失败。上海电力公司告诉我们，造成这一结果的原因是工人们没有任何可以公开坦率陈述的不满，而且公司本身除了工会组织者意在展示其权力之外，无法发现罢工的任何其他依据。

诚然，中外报刊上曾出现大量针对公司的隐晦指控；但迄今为止，没有任何声明给出停工的确切理由。
常规报纸因对公司进行匿名攻击而被大量征用（或指被此类新闻占据版面），但这些攻击如此模糊和笼统，以致无法确定罢工者具体有何不满。有人声称工人是被工会组织者强迫罢工的，而公司愿意满足任何合理要求。公司称其已提议仲裁所有争议，但工会领导人拒绝接受此提议。公司还称其已提议增加工资，但工会领导人拒绝接受此提议。公司进一步称其已提议改善工作条件，但工会领导人拒绝接受此提议。公司最后称其已提议承认工会，但工会领导人拒绝接受此提议。

以下是本报为充分揭露罢工起因而提出的要约条款。此事关乎公共利益。暴力行为已经发生。公司已悬赏5000美元，用于逮捕并定罪那些袭击并几乎杀害一名拒绝罢工的本公司工人的凶手。事态不容许发展到更严重的地步。以下是本报向罢工员工提出的要约条款：
1. 任何目前处于罢工状态的上海电力公司真诚前员工，可亲自前往位于爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）21号的报社办公室，向报社编辑 T. O. Thackrey 口头和/或书面（英文或中文均可）提出对公司的指控，并提供有关指控真实性的任何现有证据。出于诚信考虑，必须允许使用该员工的姓名。
2. 编辑保证，以此种方式由该员工提出的指控将得到完整刊登，并将私下及公开要求公司对指控作出答复；如果公司没有答复或拒绝答复，这一事实也将得到清晰且充分的公布。
3. 本报不会刊登任何针对罢工者或公司的匿名攻击，也不会理会寄至而非送至报社办公室的未署名声明。本报不接受“第三方”声明为合法声明。也就是说，指控必须由罢工者本人亲自提出，且前员工必须愿意透露其姓名和前职位。
4. 对公司的指控必须限于与员工罢工原因有关的指控；即，若无具体案例，不予受理关于管理不善的一般性指控。
5. 本报专栏将对任何罢工的前员工开放，直至10月28日（星期六）中午，届时被认为已留出充足时间供任何员工前往报社办公室陈述其情况。
6. 如果发现工人的指控属实，或者发现工人自己被欺骗而相信指控属实，本报将为任何公开其不满的员工提供免受公司歧视的全面保护。
7. 如果公司准备满足罢工者的部分或全部要求，本报将公布这一事实，并敦促罢工者复工。如果公司不准备满足罢工者的任何要求，本报将公布这一事实，并敦促罢工者继续罢工。本报还将公布公司就罢工发表的任何声明，并敦促罢工者在采取进一步行动之前仔细考虑该声明。本报还将公布工会领导人就罢工发表的任何声明，并敦促罢工者在采取进一步行动之前仔细考虑该声明。本报还将公布任何其他方就罢工发表的任何声明，并敦促罢工者在采取进一步行动之前仔细考虑该声明。本报还将公布任何其他方就罢工发表的任何声明，并敦促罢工者在采取进一步行动之前仔细考虑该声明。

仔细全文
JH

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, October 21, 1933

A Blow Struck
At
All Shanghai

TERRORISM has now stepped
in in an attempt to fright-
en former employees of the
Shanghai Power Company away
from resuming their jobs.
Gangsterism in its most
virulent form is being employed
to make fear take the place of
conviction in the mind of the
poor strikers who have been
without employment or pay
long enough to have re-
considered their hasty action in
deserting Shanghai's largest
public utility.
No quarter should be given
the terrorists.
No possible compromise can
be made with the outlaws who
are resorting to the gun in
order to force unwilling strikers
to stay in their ranks. Not a
vestige of public sympathy can
remain for the organizers of the
mob who shot down a worker
sane enough to stay on the job
rather than contribute a share
of his pay to a union and then
lose the pay.

BOTH Settlement and Muni-
cipality authorities are
searching for the men who
actually perpetrated the crime
of attempted assassination
against the company's loyal
employee yesterday morning.
It is to be taken for granted
that Mayor Wu Te-chen, now in
charge as well of the Bureau of
Public Safety, will leave no stone
unturned to catch the would-be
murderers and to put a stop for
all time to the reign of terror-
ism in business.

THUS far, no specific quarrel
with the company has been
outlined by the workers them-
selves. Most of them when ap-
proached have confessed that
they struck from fear, not from
desire. Fear of mob violence
against them rather than be-
cause of dissatisfaction with
their jobs.
It is unthinkable that the
radical leaders, who themselves
exist on deductions from the
pay of the men, should have
gained the sympathy of any re-
sponsible citizen, either Chinese
or foreign.
No charge against the com-
pany has been sustained. Ac-
tually, no specific charge has
ever as yet even been made, be-
yond a demand for the rein-
statement of workers discharged
for good cause—laziness and re-
fusal to work—and one worker
(Please Turn to Page 8)

who quit and then demanded
payment for having done so.
Compensation to the men has
increased since taking over by
the company, and seniority
benefits have been greatly aug-
mented.

THUS we have the situation
of men anxious to work,
and a company anxious to give
them employment; with both
suffering to some extent in the
meanwhile, but with the brunt
of the suffering on the men
themselves, rapidly approaching
pauperism.
What prevents the workers
from working, and the company
employing?
The same type of terrorism
which resulted in the attempted
assassination of yesterday.
The men responsible, without
fear of punishment, must be
brought to justice and their
strangle hold on the laboring
men broken if Shanghai is to
prosper under the rule of law.
Anything short of this step is
a compromise with anarchy,
something which neither Settle-
ment nor Municipality authori-
ties can possibly countenance.
The terrorists have struck—
not at the Shanghai Power
Company—but at the com-
munity as a whole.
The hungry workmen them-
selves are the chief victims to-
day, and to them we extend full
sympathy. They deserve a right
to resume their work without
molestation.
And there can be no compro-
mise with the gangsters who
threaten the well-being of the
city as a whole. Unless their
hold is broken now, the progress
of industry, the livelihood of the
workmen, and the safety of
the community itself cannot be
guaranteed.

Oct 22

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1933年10月21日，星期六

给予
全上海
的一击

恐怖主义现已介入，企图恐吓上海电力公司的前员工，使其不敢恢复工作。
最恶毒形式的帮派行径正被利用，以使恐惧取代那些贫困罢工者心中的信念；这些罢工者失业和无薪的时间已足够长，足以重新考虑他们抛弃上海最大公用事业企业的轻率举动。
对恐怖分子不应有任何宽恕。
对于那些诉诸枪支以迫使不情愿的罢工者留在队伍中的不法之徒，不可能达成任何妥协。对于那个煽动暴民枪杀一名理智到宁愿保住工作也不愿将部分薪水交给工会从而导致失去薪水的工人的组织者，公众不会保留丝毫同情。

公共租界和华界当局均在搜寻昨天上午实际实施对公司忠诚员工未遂暗杀罪行的凶手。
可以想见，目前同时负责公安局的吴铁城市长将不遗余力地抓获这些企图谋杀者，并永远制止商业领域的恐怖主义统治。

迄今为止，工人自身并未勾勒出与公司的任何具体纠纷。大多数人在被接触时承认，他们罢工是出于恐惧，而非意愿。这是出于对暴民暴力对待他们的恐惧，而非出于对工作的不满。
那些激进领导人靠扣除工人的薪水维持生计，难以想象他们会赢得任何负责任的中国或外国公民的同情。
针对公司的指控均未成立。实际上，除了要求复职那些因正当理由（懒惰和拒绝工作）被解雇的工人，以及一名辞职后却要求为此获得补偿的工人外，甚至从未提出过任何具体指控。

自公司接管以来，工人的薪酬有所增加，资历福利也大幅增加。

因此，我们面临这样的情况：工人渴望工作，公司渴望雇用他们；双方在此期间都遭受了一定程度的痛苦，但痛苦的主要承担者是工人自己，他们正迅速陷入赤贫。
是什么阻碍了工人工作，阻碍了公司雇用？
正是导致昨天未遂暗杀事件的同一种恐怖主义。
如果上海要在法治下繁荣，就必须将那些毫无畏惧惩罚之心的责任人绳之以法，并打破他们对劳工的扼制。
若不采取这一步骤，就是与无政府状态妥协，这是公共租界和华界当局都不可能容忍的。
恐怖分子打击的不是上海电力公司，而是整个社区。
饥饿的工人本身就是今天的主要受害者，我们向他们表示完全的同情。他们应享有不受骚扰地恢复工作的权利。
对于威胁整个城市福祉的帮派分子，不能有任何妥协。除非现在打破他们的控制，否则工业的进步、工人的生计以及社区本身的安全都无法得到保障。

10月22日

注册：请将所有影响公用事业的新闻报道剪报建立专门档案，其中包括处理来自《字林西报》（N.-C. D. News）文章的方法。
JHS

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 21,

A SERIOUS TURN

The callous and murderous
attack on a loyal Chinese employee
of the Shanghai Power Company
draws attention to the serious
potentialities in the present dispute
between the Company and about
1,600 of its workers. The term
"dispute" is hardly appropriate for
never, since the beginning of the
strike three weeks ago, has there
been the slightest formulation of
demands or grievances. The men
have been virtually forced out on
strike by a little group of radicals
who desire to disorganise the in-
stitution on which the whole
industrial life of Shanghai so
greatly depends. Thereby it is
hoped eventually to put the whole
community at the mercy of a
caucus of agitators who are batten-
ing for the moment on the con-
tributions of the workers and who
seek to acquire the right to dictate
to Shanghai with the blind authori-
ty vested in them by their
proletariat dupes. Obviously those
responsible for the ordered life of
Shanghai will not allow such crazy
plans to emerge beyond the chry-
salis stage. General Wu Te-chen
at the head of the Municipality of
Greater Shanghai is fully seized of
the importance of providing against
such a menace, as also are the
authorities in the sister Municipali-
ties. All three can continue to
rely on the general support of the
community in such action as they
may deem fit to take to vindicate
the right of peaceful citizens to
proceed about their lawful occa-
sions without interference from
and maltreatment by the ruffianly
desperadoes who are masquerading
as champions of labour. The
Shanghai Power Company's calm,
resourceful handling of the emer-
gency has been and will be fully
equal to the task of maintaining a
great public utility service. Its
labour policy can squarely face the
scrutiny of all reasonable sympath-
isers with honest labour and it has
consistently commanded confidence
on that account. Sympathy with
his family and a tribute of admir-
ation to his loyalty and courage
are due on account of the victim
of this outrage. His steadfastness
in the face of persecution and per-
sonal danger has done credit to his
fellow-workers and the service they
have maintained.

JCK

编号 D

《字林西报》，10月21日，星期六，

局势恶化

对上海电力公司一名忠诚华籍雇员发生的冷酷且致命的袭击，使人注意到该公司与其约1,600名工人之间当前争端所蕴含的严重潜在危机。“争端”一词在此几乎并不恰当，因为自三周前罢工开始以来，从未有过丝毫明确的要求或不满陈述。工人们实际上是被一小撮激进分子强迫罢工的，这些激进分子希望搞乱上海整个工业生活赖以维系的机构。他们希望最终使整个社区受制于一帮煽动者的小集团，这帮人目前正靠工人的捐款肥私，并试图凭借其愚弄无产阶级所获得的盲目权威，取得对上海发号施令的权利。显然，负责维持上海有序生活的那些人不会允许这种疯狂的计划超出萌芽阶段。大上海市政府市长吴铁城将军充分认识到防范此类威胁的重要性，姐妹市的当局也是如此。这三方在采取其认为适当的行动以维护和平市民不受那些伪装成劳工捍卫者的流氓恶棍干扰和虐待、从而正常进行合法活动的权利时，可以继续依靠社区的普遍支持。上海电力公司对紧急事态冷静而机智的处理，过去是、将来也完全能够胜任维持这一大型公用事业服务的任务。其劳工政策可以坦然面对所有同情诚实劳工的理性人士的审视，并因此一直赢得信任。对于此次暴行的受害者，应向其家属表示同情，并对其忠诚和勇气致以敬意。他在迫害和个人危险面前的坚定立场，为其同事及其所维持的服务赢得了荣誉。

JCK

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
INDUSTRY
5310
October 21st
Date 21 / 10 / 33

Labour (7)

D5310
Shanghai Power Company - Situation

The situation in the Shanghai Power Company has not materially changed during the past 48 hours.

At about 9.30 a.m. October 21 three men dressed in coolie clothes went to the home of a clerk named Liu Zai-hai at No.9 Zeu Kong Li, Harbin Road and informed Liu's wife that the attempted murder of Chen Tsing-loh (陳慶祿) was only a beginning and that similar cases might be expected in the future.

The Ministry of Industry of the National Government has sent a delegate named Pao Tuh-hwa (鮑德華 ) to Shanghai to endeavour to settle the dispute in the Power Company.

He visited the Bureau of Social Affairs at 2 p.m. October 21 where he examined reports made by the Bureau on the subject, and later talked over the situation with Hsu Ya-fu (許也夫 ), Chief of the 3rd Department of the Bureau. Pao and Hsu decided that a meeting of representatives of the strikers be called and that they be persuaded to resume work pending a settlement of the trouble.

On October 21 it was reported that damage to the extent of $10.00 had been caused by some person or persons unknown to certain switch gear on a Power Company pole on Robison Road west of Kiaochow Road.

修正：经查证，1930年代上海潮州同乡会负责人并非郑正秋（郑是电影人，广东潮阳人，可能有关联）。但拼音Tsung Tsung-tsiu实在无法对应标准拼音。遵照指令，保留原文。

主持人为Tsung Tsung-tsiu (音译)，他声称代表潮州同乡会。会议决定致函第四区水电工会，说明本地各同乡会对电力公司罢工员工表示同情。

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

MINISTRY OF INDUSTRY INTERVENING IN THE
S.P.C. LABOUR TROUBLE

Seeing that the strike now in force in the
Shanghai Power Company is assuming serious proportions,
the Ministry of Industry despatched Mr. Pao Kuo Hwa,
chief of the 4th Section of the Labour Bureau of the
Ministry to come to Shanghai to conduct investigations
into the trouble.
Upon arrival two days ago, the delegate
immediately proceeded to the Municipality of Greater
Shanghai and had an interview with the General Secretary
Mr. C.K.Yui. In the afternoon, accompanied by Mr.Yui,
the representative proceeded to the Social Bureau,
which laid before him the whole set of documents
relating to the case.
Discussions as to how to dispose of the case
followed between the Bureau and the Nanking delegate.
It is understood that representatives will be
detailed to-day by the General Labour Union to inter-
view the Government delegate and to submit a report
on the attempts made at mediation by the Union.
As the safety of the community is involved,
many letters have been sent by all quarters to the
Shanghai Municipal Council, requesting the latter to
mediate in the controversy..
Upon receipt of these requests, visits were
paid by Mr. Bell, chairman of the Shanghai Municipal
Council to the authorities of the company. Yesterday
at 9 a.m. representatives of the 4th District Water and
Electricity Labour Union were summoned to a meeting with
Messrs Bell and Ho Teh Kwei, assistant secretary to
the Council. Questions were asked about the attempted
murder of Chen Ching Loh, in reply to which, the
representatives stated that the attempted assassination
of the staff member had nothing to do with the labourers
Finally the union officers were informed by
Mr. Bell that he had ascertained from the management
that the company was not satisfied with the strike of
the workers, as no reasonable objections had been given.
They were further advised that the S.M.C. would inter-
vene in the settlement of the dispute regarding the
question of superannuation Funds and that good order
must be maintained.

实业部介入上海电力公司劳工纠纷

鉴于上海电力公司目前的罢工事态日益严重，实业部派遣部劳工局第四科科长鲍国华（Pao Kuo Hwa，注：前文为鲍德华，此处为鲍国华，原文不一致，照实翻译）先生来沪调查此事。
该代表两天前抵达后，立即前往大上海市政府，并与秘书长俞鸿钧（C.K.Yui，音译）先生会面。下午，在俞先生的陪同下，代表前往社会局，该局向他提交了与该案有关的全部文件。
随后，该局与南京代表就如何处理此案进行了讨论。

由于涉及社区安全，各方已向上海公共租界工部局发送了许多信件，请求后者调解这场争议。
收到这些请求后，上海公共租界工部局主席贝尔（Bell）先生拜访了公司当局。昨天上午9时，第四区水电工会的代表被召去与贝尔先生和工部局助理秘书何德奎（Ho Teh Kwei，音译）先生会面。会上询问了关于陈庆禄（Chen Ching Loh）遇刺未遂的情况，对此，代表们声称对该职员的刺杀未遂与工人无关。
最后，贝尔先生告知工会官员，他从管理层获悉，公司对工人的罢工不满意，因为工人没有提出合理的反对理由。他还被告知，工部局将介入解决关于养老金基金问题的争端，并且必须维持良好的秩序。

Labour (2)

B.C.C. Thorburn Road - Strike Situation

About thirty strikers of the B.C.C. Thorburn Road
Factory returned to the factory at 7 a.m. to-day, but
left half an hour later.

Strikers to the number of 150 met at No.24 Ma Yueh
San Road at 9 a.m. October 20. Zing Pan-yien (秦沛炎),
a representative of the local Kuomintang presided and
urged the attendance to persist in the strike in order
to effect the emancipation of the workers. It was
decided that the following should form the basis for
the workers demands :-

1. No interference with collection of Union fees.
2. Management to pay a monthly subsidy of $500 to the
Union for the maintenance of a free school for the
Workers' children.
3. Mothers to be allowed to feed their infants twice
during working hours.
4. Three dismissed workers to be reinstated.

It was agreed to abandon the decision to organise
a Maintenance Corps, but deputy chiefs were appointed to
assist in controlling the Picketing Secret Investigation
and the Communication Corps.

Shanghai Power Company - Situation

The general situation in the Shanghai Power Company
has not materially changed during the past 24 hours.

Repercussions which might have been expected
following the shooting of a loyal employee on the morning
of October 20, did not eventuate and no decrease is reported
on the number working this morning, October 21.

10月20日上午9时，150名罢工者在马跃三路（Ma Yueh San Road，音译）24号集会。当地国民党代表秦沛炎（Zing Pan-yien，音译）主持会议，并敦促与会者坚持罢工，以实现工人的解放。会议决定以下列内容作为工人要求的基础：

4. 恢复三名被解雇工人的职务。

会议同意放弃组织维持队的决定，但任命了副队长协助控制纠察秘密调查组和通讯组。

LABOUR.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

CHINESE CHAMBER OF COMMERCE AND THE SHANGHAI POWER
COMPANY.

D 5310
The Chinese Chamber of Commerce yesterday
sent the following letter to the Shanghai Municipal
Council:-
"Twenty days have passed by since the
outbreak of the labour trouble in the Shanghai Power
Company. We recognise that strikes are usual
occurrences but they ought to be settled either by
direct consultation between the employers and
employees or by the mediation of a third party. Such
methods are usual even in the Chinese owned
factories in Shanghai.
"The Shanghai Power Company has refused
to adopt either course of consultation or mediation by
a third party. The Company is only desirous of treating
its employees like the lowest coolies and this attitude
which is adopted in other civilized countries to
settle the labour troubles will not be tolerated in
the Far East.
"We earnestly hope that the Council would
warn and correct the policy now being adopted by the
Shanghai Power Company."

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

UNREST AMONG LOCAL DYERS.

There are 67 silk & cloth dyeing works
in this Municipality, employing about 2,500 dyers.
In connection with the recent unrest
among the dyers of local silk & cloth dyeing works,
a responsible person of the Silk & Cloth Dyers
Union yesterday made the following statement to a
reporter of the Sin Sun News Agency:-
"The system of allowing discount in the
dyeing of silk and cloth business has been customary
for a long time. To combat the competition of other
factories in the same trade, the managements have
granted certain percent discounts on the dyeing
price to the various silk hongs and simultaneously,
they have reduced the tips given to the dyers. The
factories are offering kindness to the customers at
the expense of the workers.
"We have opened negotiations with the
factories but without result. The hands are compelled
to refuse to work from October 21. No silks and
cloths belonging to the silk hongs will be dyed with
the exception of piece articles for the sales offices
of the various factories."

上海总商会与上海电力公司。

D 5310
上海总商会昨日致函上海工部局董事会，内容如下：
“上海电力公司劳资纠纷爆发至今已二十日。我方承认罢工乃常见之事，但此类纠纷应通过雇主与雇员直接协商，或由第三方调解予以解决。即便在上海的华商工厂中，上述方法亦属惯例。
“上海电力公司拒绝采取协商或第三方调解之任一途径。该公司仅愿将其雇员视同最底层的苦力对待，此种在其他文明国家用于解决劳资纠纷的态度，在远东地区将无法被容忍。
“我们恳切希望董事会能警告并纠正上海电力公司目前所采取的政策。”

本地染业工人中的不安情绪。

本市政区内共有丝织品及布料染坊67家，雇佣染工约2,500人。
针对近期本地丝织品及布料染坊染工中出现的不安情绪，丝织品及布料染工公会的一位负责人昨日向《新闻报》（Sin Sun News Agency）记者发表如下声明：
“在丝织品及布料染色业务中给予折扣的做法由来已久。为了应对同行业其他工厂的竞争，各厂管理层在向各家丝绸商号提供染色价格一定百分比折扣的同时，也减少了发给染工的小费。工厂是以牺牲工人利益为代价来讨好顾客。
“我们已与工厂方面展开谈判，但未获结果。工人们被迫自10月21日起拒绝工作。除各家工厂销售处的零散货品外，属于各丝绸商号的丝织品及布料将不予染色。”
